literal: Wei Imperial Clan
idiomatic: The Wei Imperial Clan

literal: Duke of Shanggu Heluo was a great-grandson of Emperor Shenyuan.
idiomatic: Duke of Shanggu Heluo was a great-grandson of Emperor Shenyuan.

literal: At first he followed Emperor Daowu from the Du Gu clan to the Helan tribe; with his younger brother Jian he urged Helan Ne to raise Daowu as chief.
idiomatic: Early on he followed Emperor Daowu from the Du Gu clan to the Helan tribe, and together with his younger brother Jian persuaded Helan Ne to set Daowu up as leader.

literal: When Daowu took the throne, for meritorious support he and Jian were enfeoffed as dukes on the same day.
idiomatic: Once Daowu ascended the throne, both were enfeoffed as dukes the same day for their aid in raising him.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Ti was enfeoffed Duke of Xiangcheng, later advanced to prince.
idiomatic: His son Ti received the title Duke of Xiangcheng and was later promoted to prince.

literal: Attacking Murong Lin at Yitai, he was struck by a stray arrow and died.
idiomatic: While attacking Murong Lin at Yitai he took a stray arrow and died.

literal: The emperor, because Grand Physician Yin Guang's treatment had not exhausted every art, had him executed.
idiomatic: The emperor had Grand Physician Yin Guang executed, holding that his treatment had not exhausted every possible remedy.

literal: His son Xi inherited the title, was demoted to Duke of Xiangcheng, died, and was posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng.
idiomatic: His son Xi inherited the rank, was demoted to Duke of Xiangcheng, died, and was posthumously ennobled Prince of Xiangcheng.

literal: After Shenyuan there were also Duke of Jiande Yingwen and Marquis of Zhending Lu, both serving Emperor Taiwu and specially receiving enfeoffments.
idiomatic: Shenyuan's line also produced Duke of Jiande Yingwen and Marquis of Zhending Lu, who both served Emperor Taiwu and were specially enfeoffed.

literal: Marquis of Wuling Yin and Prince of Changle Shoule were both descendants of Emperor Zhang.
idiomatic: Marquis of Wuling Yin and Prince of Changle Shoule were both descendants of Emperor Zhang.

literal: Yin followed Daowu in pacifying the Central Plains and was enfeoffed Marquis of Qu Ni for merit.
idiomatic: Yin followed Daowu in pacifying the Central Plains and was enfeoffed Marquis of Qu Ni for his service.

literal: Under Emperor Taiwu his title was changed to Marquis of Wuling.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu his fief was changed to Marquis of Wuling.

literal: Shoule held the posts of Director of the Bureau of Selection and Prince of Nan'an; his title was changed to Prince of Changle.
idiomatic: Shoule served as Director of the Bureau of Selection and Prince of Nan'an before his title was changed to Prince of Changle.

literal: When Emperor Wencheng succeeded, Shoule had merit in supporting the enthronement and was appointed Grand Preceptor, Grand Commander of All Armies Within and Without, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, Shoule was rewarded for aiding the succession with the posts of Grand Preceptor, Grand Commander of All Armies Within and Without, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Boasting of his merit, he struggled for power with Director of the Masters of Writing Changsun Kehou; both were executed.
idiomatic: He flaunted his achievements and clashed with Director of the Masters of Writing Changsun Kehou over power; both men were executed.

literal: Duke of Wangdu Tui was a descendant of Emperor Zhao.
idiomatic: Duke of Wangdu Tui was a descendant of Emperor Zhao.

literal: He followed Daowu in pacifying the Central Plains and was enfeoffed Marquis of Wangdu.
idiomatic: He followed Daowu in pacifying the Central Plains and received the title Marquis of Wangdu.

literal: Emperor Taiwu, because Tui had handsome features and dignified bearing, sent him to welcome the Left Lady of Brilliant Deportment from the Rouran and advanced his title to duke.
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu, finding Tui handsome and dignified in bearing, sent him to escort the Left Lady of Brilliant Deportment from the Rouran and promoted him to duke.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Marquis of Quyang Suyan, Duke of Shunyang Yu, and Prince of Yidu Muchen were all descendants of Emperor Huan.
idiomatic: Marquis of Quyang Suyan, Duke of Shunyang Yu, and Prince of Yidu Muchen were all descendants of Emperor Huan.

literal: Suyan followed Daowu as a junior commander in campaigns against the tribes; when Bing Province was first secured he became its governor.
idiomatic: Suyan served Daowu as a junior commander in campaigns against the tribes; after Bing Province was first secured he was made its governor.

literal: When Daowu was alarmed at Baixi, the Bingzhou garrison commander Feng Douzhen rebelled; Suyan beheaded him.
idiomatic: When Daowu was alarmed at Baixi, the Bingzhou garrison commander Feng Douzhen rebelled, and Suyan beheaded him.

literal: At the time Daowu wished to soothe and please the newly submitted; regretting the massacre at Canhe, yet Suyan had killed too many and was removed from office.
idiomatic: Daowu then wished to win over the newly submitted and regretted the massacre at Canhe, but Suyan had slaughtered too many people and was dismissed.

literal: When Zhongshan was pacified he was appointed Governor of You Province; extravagant and dissolute, he was demoted to Governor of Shanggu.
idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell he was made Governor of You Province, but his extravagance and dissipation earned him demotion to Governor of Shanggu.

literal: Later he was enfeoffed Marquis of Quyang.
idiomatic: He was later enfeoffed Marquis of Quyang.

literal: At the time Daowu attended to Huang-Lao teachings and wished to purify customs by simple example;
idiomatic: Daowu was then devoted to Huang-Lao teachings and wished to reform customs through pure example;

literal: even carriage fittings and personal adornments were stripped of carving.
idiomatic: even imperial carriage fittings and personal adornments were stripped of ornament.

literal: Suyan's extravagance exceeded all bounds; the emperor deeply resented it, accumulated his offenses, and on summoning him had him sentenced to death.
idiomatic: Suyan's extravagance knew no bounds; the emperor nursed a deep grudge, tallied his offenses, and when he was summoned had him put to death.

literal: Yu from youth was loyal, upright, and unbending.
idiomatic: From youth Yu was loyal, upright, and unyielding.

literal: Under Emperor Wencheng he was Palace Director of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed Duke of Shunyang.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng he served as Palace Director of the Masters of Writing and was enfeoffed Duke of Shunyang.

literal: When Wencheng died, Yichun held sole power; Yu entered through the Shunde Gate intending to kill Yichun.
idiomatic: After Wencheng's death Yichun seized sole power; Yu entered by the Shunde Gate intending to kill him.

literal: Yichun, cornered and terrified, thereupon installed Emperor Xianwen to hold court.
idiomatic: Cornered and terrified, Yichun thereupon installed Emperor Xianwen to hold court.

literal: Later he again plotted to kill Yichun and was executed by Yichun.
idiomatic: He later plotted again to kill Yichun and was executed by him.

literal: Emperor Xianwen recorded Yu's loyal uprightness, posthumously enfeoffed him Prince of Shunyang, posthumous name Jian.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen honored Yu's loyal uprightness, posthumously making him Prince of Shunyang with the temple name Jian.

literal: Muchen, when Wencheng succeeded, successively served as Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and was enfeoffed Duke of Nanping.
idiomatic: When Wencheng took the throne Muchen served successively as Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and was enfeoffed Duke of Nanping.

literal: When Yichun plotted rebellion, Muchen and the Duke of Shunyang plotted to kill him.
idiomatic: When Yichun plotted rebellion, Muchen and the Duke of Shunyang conspired to kill him.

literal: When the affair broke out, Muchen escaped.
idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Muchen escaped.

literal: When Xianwen transmitted the throne, he had merit in fixing the succession plan.
idiomatic: When Xianwen abdicated in favor of a successor, he had merit in settling the succession.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowen succeeded, Muchen was advanced to Prince of Yidu, dismissed as Governor of Yong Province, and stationed at Chang'an.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was promoted to Prince of Yidu, relieved as Governor of Yong Province, and posted at Chang'an.

literal: Guilty of an offense, he was executed and his title extinguished.
idiomatic: Convicted of a crime, he was executed and his title was extinguished.

literal: Liuxiu was the eldest son of Emperor Mu.
idiomatic: Liuxiu was the eldest son of Emperor Mu.

literal: From youth he was fierce and perverse.
idiomatic: From youth he was violent and rebellious.

literal: In the fifth year of Emperor Mu he sent Liuxiu with the assisting minister Wei Xiong, Fan Ban, and Ji Dan and others to rescue Liu Kun, while the emperor personally commanded a great army as rear support.
idiomatic: In Emperor Mu's fifth year he sent Liuxiu with the assisting minister Wei Xiong, Fan Ban, Ji Dan, and others to rescue Liu Kun, while he personally led a great army in support.

literal: Liu Can was afraid, broke out and fled, and very many were killed and wounded.
idiomatic: Liu Can, in fear, broke out and fled; the dead and wounded were very many.

literal: The emperor then held a great hunt on Shouyang Mountain, displayed skin and flesh for review, and the mountain turned red.
idiomatic: The emperor then held a great hunt on Shouyang Mountain, laid out hides and flesh for inspection, and the mountain turned red.

literal: Emperor Mu's youngest son Biyan was favored; he wished to make him heir;
idiomatic: The emperor's youngest son Biyan was favored, and he wished to make him heir;

literal: Liuxiu was sent out to dwell at Xinping city while his mother was demoted.
idiomatic: Liuxiu was sent to live at Xinping while his mother was cast down.

literal: Liuxiu had a piebald thoroughbred that could travel five hundred li in a day; Emperor Mu wished to take it to give to Biyan.
idiomatic: Liuxiu owned a piebald thoroughbred that could run five hundred li in a day; Emperor Mu wished to take it for Biyan.

literal: Later when Liuxiu came to court, Emperor Mu again ordered him to bow to Biyan; Liuxiu refused.
idiomatic: When Liuxiu later came to court, Emperor Mu again ordered him to bow to Biyan, but Liuxiu refused.

literal: Emperor Mu then seated Biyan on the step carriage he himself rode and had men guide him out on an excursion.
idiomatic: The emperor then seated Biyan on his own step carriage and had attendants escort him on an outing.

literal: Liuxiu saw him from afar, thought it was Emperor Mu, and bowed prostrate at the roadside;
idiomatic: Liuxiu saw the procession from afar, mistook it for the emperor, and prostrated himself by the road;

literal: when he drew near and found it was Biyan, he left in shame and rage.
idiomatic: when he drew near and found it was only Biyan, he left in shame and fury.

literal: Emperor Mu was angry and attacked him.
idiomatic: The emperor, enraged, marched against him.

literal: The imperial army fared ill; Liuxiu killed Biyan.
idiomatic: The imperial army fared poorly; Liuxiu killed Biyan.

literal: The emperor changed clothes and walked among the people in disguise; a low woman recognized him, and he suddenly died.
idiomatic: The emperor disguised himself among commoners; a humble woman recognized him, and he died suddenly.

literal: Emperor Huan's son Pugen had been guarding abroad; hearing of the crisis he came and destroyed Liuxiu.
idiomatic: Emperor Huan's son Pugen had been guarding abroad; hearing of the crisis he came and destroyed Liuxiu.

literal: Baron of Jiyang Bigan and Duke of Jiangxia Lü were both Daowu's younger cousins.
idiomatic: Baron of Jiyang Bigan and Duke of Jiangxia Lü were both younger cousins of Daowu.

literal: Bigan, as Director of Palace Guards, attacked the Dingling of Baixian with merit and was enfeoffed Baron of Jiyang.
idiomatic: As Director of Palace Guards, Bigan attacked the Dingling of Baixian with success and was enfeoffed Baron of Jiyang.

literal: Later he was Commander of the Southern Route and died in battle.
idiomatic: He later served as Commander of the Southern Route and died in battle.

literal: Lü was enfeoffed Duke of Jiangxia for military merit, held the post of Grand Officer of the Outer Court, and was greatly respected.
idiomatic: Lü was enfeoffed Duke of Jiangxia for military merit, served as Grand Officer of the Outer Court, and was held in high esteem.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Prince of Jiangxia, buried at Jinling.
idiomatic: He died, was posthumously made Prince of Jiangxia, and was buried at Jinling.

literal: Prince of Gaoliang Gu was the fourth son of Emperor Pingwen.
idiomatic: Prince of Gaoliang Gu was the fourth son of Emperor Pingwen.

literal: Many talents and arts; resolute will and strategy.
idiomatic: He had many talents and arts, and possessed resolute will and strategy.

literal: In the first year before Emperor Lie, the state had internal strife and Zhaocheng went to Xiangguo.
idiomatic: In the year before Emperor Lie's reign the state suffered internal strife and Zhaocheng went to Xiangguo.

literal: Later when Emperor Lie was near death, he entrusted the command to welcome and establish Zhaocheng.
idiomatic: When Emperor Lie was dying he entrusted the command to welcome and establish Zhaocheng.

literal: When he died, the ministers all said that with a great recent calamity Zhaocheng's coming could not yet be settled upon; they should establish the eldest prince.
idiomatic: At his death the ministers argued that with so recent a calamity Zhaocheng's arrival could not yet be assured; they ought to establish the eldest prince.

literal: The next younger brother Qu was fierce and changeable—not like Gu's breadth, harmony, and compliance.
idiomatic: The next younger brother Qu was fierce and changeable—unlike Gu's breadth, harmony, and compliance.

literal: Thereupon the elders Liang Gai and others killed Qu and together raised Gu.
idiomatic: Thereupon the elders Liang Gai and others killed Qu and together raised Gu.

literal: He would not accept; he went in person to Ye to welcome Zhaocheng, asked to remain himself as hostage, and Shi Jilong, moved by righteousness, consented.
idiomatic: He refused; he went in person to Ye to welcome Zhaocheng, offered to remain as hostage, and Shi Jilong, moved by his righteousness, agreed.

literal: When Zhaocheng took the royal title, he divided half the state and gave it to him.
idiomatic: When Zhaocheng took the royal title he divided half the realm and gave it to him.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Jin, losing office and nursing anger, incited Shijun to rebel and died at Chang'an.
idiomatic: His son Jin, embittered after losing office, incited Shijun to rebel and died at Chang'an.

literal: Under Daowu, because Gu's merit was high, he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Gaoliang, posthumous name Shenwu.
idiomatic: Under Daowu, Gu's merit being great, he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Gaoliang with the temple name Shenwu.

literal: Jin's son Zhenle had repeated battle merit and later inherited his grandfather's fief.
idiomatic: Jin's son Zhenle won repeated battle honors and later inherited his grandfather's title.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Mingyuan he was changed to Prince of Pingyang.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Mingyuan's reign his title was changed to Prince of Pingyang.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Li inherited the original title Prince of Gaoliang.
idiomatic: His son Li inherited the original title, Prince of Gaoliang.

literal: He died; posthumous name Prince Yi.
idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous name Prince Yi.

literal: His son Na inherited the title, was appointed Grand Officer of the Central Court, fierce and skilled in attack and battle.
idiomatic: His son Na inherited the title, was appointed Grand Officer of the Central Court, and was fierce and skilled in assault.

literal: At the beginning of Zhengping he was executed for an offense.
idiomatic: At the start of Zhengping he was executed for an offense.

literal: When Xianwen succeeded, recalling Na's merit, he ordered his son He to inherit the fief.
idiomatic: When Xianwen took the throne he recalled Na's merit and ordered his son He to inherit the fief.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Dacao was by nature simple and upright.
idiomatic: His son Dacao was by nature plainspoken and upright.

literal: Under Xiaowen, princes who were not descendants of Daowu were by rule demoted to duke.
idiomatic: Under Xiaowen, princes who were not Daowu's descendants were by rule demoted to duke.

literal: Because Dacao's forebears had yielded the state with heavy merit and Gaozu's Zhenle had outstanding merit in the former dynasty, he was changed to Duke of Taiyuan commandery.
idiomatic: Because his forebears had yielded the realm with great merit and Gaozu's Zhenle had shone in the previous dynasty, he was changed to Duke of Taiyuan commandery.

literal: He died without sons; the state was extinguished.
idiomatic: He died without heirs and the fief was extinguished.

literal: Emperor Xuanwu again had Dacao's cousin's son Hongwei continue the line.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu again had Dacao's cousin's son Hongwei continue the line.

literal: Respectful and humble, fond of learning, he was Governor of Yingchuan and had administrative achievements.
idiomatic: Respectful and studious, he served as Governor of Yingchuan with administrative distinction.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing he gathered men at Yingchuan in response to Western Wei; Qi Shenwu sent generals to suppress and pacify him.
idiomatic: At the start of Xiaojing he gathered followers at Yingchuan in support of Western Wei; Qi Shenwu sent generals who suppressed and pacified him.

literal: Li's younger brother Ling was enfeoffed Baron of Xiangyi by Taiwu and advanced to viscount.
idiomatic: Li's younger brother Ling was enfeoffed Baron of Xiangyi by Taiwu and later advanced to viscount.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Daqi inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Daqi inherited the title.

literal: Later he plotted with Yuan Jin to harm Qi Wenxiang and was killed.
idiomatic: He later plotted with Yuan Jin to harm Qi Wenxiang and was killed.

literal: Gu's grandson Du, at the beginning of Daowu, was enfeoffed Marquis of Songzi and was Director of the Bureau of Review.
idiomatic: Gu's grandson Du, at the start of Daowu, was enfeoffed Marquis of Songzi and served as Director of the Bureau of Review.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Yijin inherited the title Marquis of Xiangyang.
idiomatic: His son Yijin inherited the title Marquis of Xiangyang.

literal: Xianwen honored old worthies and appointed him Grand Officer of the Outer Court, treating him with great favor.
idiomatic: Xianwen honored old worthies, appointed him Grand Officer of the Outer Court, and treated him with exceptional favor.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Ping, style Chuguo, inherited the hereditary title Marquis of Songzi and for military merit was also given Baron of Ailing.
idiomatic: His son Ping, style Chuguo, inherited the hereditary Marquisate of Songzi and for military merit was also granted Baron of Ailing.
